response.record_grain: One record per OCDS release in the top-level releases array; a release is a publication event and may nest multiple parties, awards, contracts, items and suppliers.
response.grain_rationale: The reader record_path is releases, so each row is one release. Contracts, awards and suppliers remain nested and are not expanded; the supplier and procuring-entity parties are selected by the roles discriminator bindings, which refuse multiple matches rather than silently picking one.

record_id.rationale: releases[].id identifies exactly one published release, which is the row grain. The engine uses a content hash for source_record_id regardless of this strategy.

fields.rationale: The publisher states one party name for the supplier and does not distinguish registered from trading names. entity.legal_name is defined as the registered legal name, so this reuse is a bounded approximation: the emitted value is a published party name, not a registrar-stated legal name, and no current_legal_name claim_scope is set. Downstream consumers must not treat it as authoritative registered-name evidence. No legal form is inferred from forms such as 'The Trustee for ... Trust', 'Data#3 Limited', 'RMI Cleaning Services, LLC' or 'MILES AND STOCKBRIDGE P.C.'.

The supplier party's additional identifier is an ABN only when the scheme is AU-ABN; the abn transform enforces the 11-digit checksum. An ABN is an identifier only and proves nothing about legal form. Absence of an ABN (e.g. a supplier with no additionalIdentifiers) is an abstention, not evidence the supplier has no ABN.
The locality of the supplier party's own stated address.

The region of the supplier party's stated address, normalised to the state enum. Non-Australian regions (e.g. 'Outside Australia') are coerced to OTHER, which conflates all non-Australian regions and loses the raw text; the emitted OTHER means 'not an Australian state/territory', not a location, and must not be read as an Australian state.
The postal code of the supplier party's stated address, kept as written; foreign postcodes are not asserted to be Australian.
The country of the supplier party's stated address as written.

The publisher states one party name for the procuring entity and does not distinguish registered from trading names. entity.legal_name is defined as the registered legal name, so this reuse is a bounded approximation: the emitted value is a published party name, not a registrar-stated legal name, and no current_legal_name claim_scope is set.
The procuring entity's additional identifier is an ABN only when the scheme is AU-ABN; the abn transform enforces the checksum.
The locality of the procuring entity's own stated address.
The region of the procuring entity's stated address, normalised to the state enum; OTHER means 'not an Australian state/territory'.
The postal code of the procuring entity's stated address.

The publisher's contract notice identifier. It is not a supplier key, ABN or ACN. It is not unique per release: an amendment release (tag 'contractAmendment') restates the original notice id, so the contract role key contracts[0].id collides across the original and amendment releases and the amendment release is not distinguishable by the contract key alone. The engine's named-role identity may repeat across records, so this is a bounded identity limitation, not an overwrite.
The date the contract was signed as stated. The concept is a date, so the stated time of day is not preserved; it is not the start date, publication date or registration date.

The first day of the contract period. The source states a full timestamp whose time component is not constant across rows (e.g. 14:00Z on some rows, 13:00Z on others), so no fixed local-midnight convention can be assumed. The parse_date transform truncates the time, so the emitted value is the UTC date component of the stated timestamp; the local contract day may differ by one. It is not the release publication date and not the moment the notice was observed.

The last day of the contract period, i.e. the planned end of this contract's term. The source states a full timestamp whose time component is not constant across rows (e.g. 13:00Z observed), so no fixed local-midnight convention can be assumed. The parse_date transform truncates the time, so the emitted value is the UTC date component of the stated timestamp; the local contract day may differ by one. It is not a licence expiry and not a business's cessation.
The scope of work as the procuring entity described it. It describes this procurement, not the supplier's company-wide industry or sector.
The total maximum contract value over its life, qualified by the stated ISO 4217 currency. It is not annual expenditure, revenue or business income.

The contract status as reported at extraction, using the OCDS contract status codelist with unknown for anything not published. Only 'active' is observed; it is not the supplier's registration status.

The classification code of the first contracted item, paired with the publisher's scheme (UNSPSC). It describes the goods or services bought, not the supplier's company-wide industry. Additional items are not captured at this grain.
How the contract was let, using the OCDS procurement method codelist. It describes the procurement process only and says nothing about contract size, supplier capability or the notice population.

Whether the notice marks the limited tender as exempt, published as 1 or 0 and mapped to true/false; a blank value is unknown, never false. Both 'true' (from raw '1') and 'false' (from raw '0') are observed in this snapshot; 'unknown' is codelist-derived, not observed.

The exemption clause code the publisher gives for a limited tender, kept as stated. It refers to a Commonwealth procurement exemption clause; the separate verbatim reason text is captured by dyn.contract.limited_tender_reason and is not assumed to quote this code. Observed on one row only in this snapshot; the mapping is verified on that row (emitted value 'TR', no value errors), but coverage is limited to that single observation.

The publisher's full wording of the reason a limited tender was used, kept verbatim as source evidence with its clause numbering and headings. It is a reported justification, not an assessment made by us. Observed on one row only in this snapshot; the mapping is verified on that row (verbatim reason text emitted, no value errors), but coverage is limited to that single observation.

supplier.rationale: The party bound by roles=supplier is the awarded supplier business. Its publisher party id is the role key; it is not a legal identifier.

procuring_entity.rationale: The party bound by roles=procuringEntity is the government buyer business. Its publisher party id is the role key; it is not a legal identifier.

contract.rationale: The contract notice identified by contracts[0].id is the contract entity for this release. An amendment release restates the same notice id, so this key collides across the original and amendment releases and the amendment release is not distinguishable by the contract key alone; the engine's named-role identity may repeat across records, so this is a bounded identity limitation, not an overwrite.

relationships.rationale: The contract notice names the role-bound supplier party as an awarded supplier. The edge emits when both the contract role and the role-bound supplier party have emitted claims; the config executes no extra equality guard, so a divergence between the award supplier id (awards[0].suppliers[0].id) and the role-bound supplier party id (parties[].id where roles includes supplier) is not detected by the config. If the supplier binding refuses because multiple parties carry the supplier role, no edge is emitted. An award may name several suppliers and each must be linked separately, never collapsed into one.

The contract notice names the role-bound procuring entity party as the buyer. The edge emits when both the contract role and the role-bound procuring entity party have emitted claims. The role is a procurement role in this process and does not by itself establish legal form, ownership or company-wide scope.

unmapped.reason: Amendment fields ARE present on at least one amendment release (held-out ordinal 19, tag 'contractAmendment', contracts[0].amendments[0].id = 'CN4280171-A1'), so the earlier 'not present in the inspected snapshot' reason was inaccurate. Left unmapped because (a) only a single amendment observation exists, (b) there is no amendment entity type in the ontology, and (c) the contract key contracts[0].id collides across the original and amendment releases as already disclosed in dyn.contract.notice_number. No amendment concept is proposed from a single held-out row.

Observed on at least one amendment release (held-out ordinal 19, tag 'contractAmendment', value 'prod-2416a68113334cca9867238cb761658c-8ea45a4cba6b302f9a4c4cc4babc2319'), so the earlier 'not present in the inspected snapshot' reason was inaccurate. Left unmapped because only one observation exists, there is no amendment entity type, and the contract key contracts[0].id collides across original and amendment releases as disclosed in dyn.contract.notice_number. No amendment-link concept is proposed from a single held-out row.

Observed on at least one amendment release (held-out ordinal 19, tag 'contractAmendment', value 'prod-2416a68113334cca9867238cb761658c-927300ea26db3e1e8fb91d355fbcc4fe'), so the earlier 'not present in the inspected snapshot' reason was inaccurate. Left unmapped because only one observation exists, there is no amendment entity type, and the contract key contracts[0].id collides across original and amendment releases as disclosed in dyn.contract.notice_number. No amendment concept is proposed from a single held-out row.

roles is the discriminator used to bind supplier_party and procuring_entity_party; its meaning is already carried by the CONTRACT_AWARDED_TO and CONTRACT_PROCURED_BY relationships, so a separate role claim would duplicate them.
roles is the discriminator used to bind the procuring entity party; its meaning is already carried by CONTRACT_PROCURED_BY, so a separate role claim would duplicate it.

An opaque publisher party key with no business meaning. ABN is the published identifier where available, and a source-specific party key concept would duplicate identity without adding evidence; it must never be treated as a legal identifier.
An opaque publisher party key with no business meaning; it must never be treated as a legal identifier.

Held-out rows show the supplier party's contactPoint is the buyer's boilerplate (e.g. a Marshall Islands supplier carrying procurement@niaa.gov.au), so mapping it to the supplier entity would assert a wrong-entity email. Unmapped rather than attached to the wrong business.

Held-out rows show the supplier party's contactPoint telephone is the buyer's boilerplate (e.g. '02 6261 1111' on a foreign supplier), so mapping it to the supplier entity would assert a wrong-entity phone. Unmapped rather than attached to the wrong business.

The procuring entity publishes a role mailbox (tenders@finance.gov.au), but the role_email transform classifies it as a personal mailbox and drops it (18/18 dropped in validation). Rather than claim a concept that silently discards the value, the field is unmapped and the transform misclassification is recorded as a finding.

ocid identifies an OCDS contracting process or package that can span multiple releases, awards and contracts, not a single contract or supplier. At this one-release-per-row grain the release id already keys the record and there is no contracting-process entity type.
tender.id repeats the ocid in this snapshot, so it is a process-level key rather than a tender or contract identifier.
A human-readable restatement of procurementMethod ('Limited tender', 'Open tender'); storing both would create a redundant alias of dyn.contract.procurement_method.

In this snapshot title holds short internal reference strings (e.g. NCD11811, 4600030790) that look like agency references rather than descriptive titles; mapping it would create a second identifier concept indistinguishable from dyn.contract.notice_number.
A local join key from contract to award inside the release, not a business fact; the supplier link it supports is already recorded by CONTRACT_AWARDED_TO.
A local award identifier scoped to the release and publisher, not a business identifier and not stable across sources.
Award status uses a separate OCDS codelist and in this snapshot merely repeats contracts[0].status; mapping both would create two competing status claims for one notice until they are reconciled.

In the observed non-amendment rows the award date equals the contract dateSigned, so it adds no separate business fact there; on amendment releases it does not equal the release date, so it is not a publication timestamp either. A third competing date for one notice would be misleading. This is a bounded coverage choice based on observed rows, not a claim that the two dates are always equal.
A denormalised restatement of the supplier party id; the supplier link is already carried by CONTRACT_AWARDED_TO and the party binding, so a separate claim would duplicate identity.
A denormalised restatement of parties[].name for the same supplier; mapping both would double-count one name claim.
An internal item identifier local to the release; it is not a business identifier and adds nothing beyond the item classification code already captured.

contactPoint.name mixes organisational unit labels ('FINANCE DIVISION', 'Procurement', 'CONTRACTS OFFICER') with personal names ('Sandra Tuck'). The ontology has no concept for a contact's unit, and personal names must not be stored, so these are dropped rather than mapped.
A contact organisational branch label for the party (e.g. 'Budget and Policy Branch'), not a business fact and not a concept in the current ontology.
A contact organisational division label for the party (e.g. 'FINANCE DIVISION'), not a business fact and not a concept in the current ontology.
A single street-address line (e.g. 'PO Box 3'), often a post-office box. address.full expects a complete formatted address and concatenating lines would invent structure the source does not state.
A single street-address line for a government agency; the same objection as for supplier street addresses applies, and address.full is not a street-line concept.
Not published for the procuring entity party in this snapshot; the column profile shows no nonempty values, so no country claim can be made without inventing data.
Not published for the procuring entity party in this snapshot; no phone claim can be made without inventing data.
Constant ('contract') schema metadata describing the OCDS release stage, not a business fact; the contract entity already carries that meaning.
Constant ('tender') OCDS schema metadata describing how the process was initiated, with no business fact about the supplier or the contract.
A document language tag ('EN') for the release payload, not a claim about any business or contract.

response.notes: Revision: the three amendment unmapped reasons now state that contracts[0].amendments[0].id / releaseID / amendsReleaseID ARE observed on at least one amendment release (held-out ordinal 19, tag 'contractAmendment', contracts[0].id 'CN4280171') and explain why they remain unmapped: a single observation, no amendment entity type, and the contract key collision already disclosed in dyn.contract.notice_number. No amendment concept is proposed from a single held-out row. The contract entity type and the remaining contract concepts are unchanged. The supplier and procuring-entity party ids are used only as role keys, not as legal identifiers. Contract value is a reported maximum over the contract life, not annual expenditure or business income. UNSPSC item classification is not the supplier's company-wide industry. ABNs are checksum-validated and prove nothing about legal form.
